**Test image observations:**
- Soybean leaf showing the underside (abaxial surface)
- Overall grayish-blue/silvery coating across the leaf surface
- Small yellowish-green spots/lesions scattered on the surface
- The grayish appearance suggests fungal sporulation on the leaf underside

**Candidate analysis:**
- **Downy mildew**: Classic symptom is pale yellow spots on upper surface with grayish-white sporulation on lower leaf surface — matches the grayish coating seen
- **Soybean rust**: Shows distinct tan-brown pustules (uredinia) on leaf undersides — not visible here
- **Soybean Dwarf Mosaic Virus**: Would show mosaic/mottling patterns — not seen here

The grayish-blue sporulation coating on what appears to be the underside of the leaf, combined with the small yellowish lesion spots, strongly matches Downy mildew. The soybean rust reference image shows brown rust-colored pustules which are absent in the test image.
